exposure.statement: TWI for aluminium established by the AFC Panel.
Foods with very high mean aluminium concentrations include tea leaves, herbs, cocoa and cocoa products, and spices.

Swedish duplicate-diet study (Jorhem and Haegglund, 1992): major contributor to Al exposure was a chocolate-mint cake made with an acidic sodium aluminium phosphate baking mix (additive, not cocoa itself).

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary says cocoa has 'no single anchor reported in the opinion'; the opinion's Annex Table 2 prints cocoa, cocoa products mean 33 mg/kg (range 9.4-103 mg/kg fresh weight) from Müller et al. (1998), and French TDS chocolate 3.7 mg/kg.
unresolved: Number of cocoa samples in Müller et al. (1998) not given in the opinion; values are secondary and should be taken from the primary paper if in corpus.
